rows.why: Rule 1 is silent almost everywhere in this diffuse all-flat event, and 62078 is the only vertex with a genuine rise-away segment (62052 climbs monotonically to 129k at 62076, so that particle stopped elsewhere) plus it is a 4-prong star; the 27 cm cluster 48 sits 26 cm upstream with every segment flat, so this is close to a guess.

Textbook rule 1: both attached segments rise away from 16002 - a 171 cm muon cooling from 122704 at its stopping end and an 81 cm proton cooling from a 198843 Bragg tip - and it is also the lowest-z candidate in the event.

Rule 1 at 19002: a 79.8 cm muon rises away to a 108269 stopping end and an 8.4 cm heavy prong rises away to 134111, i.e. two particles both stop elsewhere; the competing 3/3-rise-away vertex 49023 is 14 cm downstream and its arms are short sub-MIP shower prongs.

The 172.8 cm muon is flat at ~50000 over its whole length with no Bragg rise at either end (p4), so it exits at the y=199 top boundary and must START at the interior end 5001, where a 1.5 cm 145506 e/cm proton stub is attached.
The single 91 cm muon rises away from 12001 to a 115217 stopping end at 12000, both ends are interior so the track is contained, and 12001 additionally carries a 0.6 cm proton stub.
Rule 1 plus a 3-prong star: a 16.1 cm proton leaves 13002 and stops at 13000 with a clean 124046 -> 203053 Bragg rise, and two further short heavy stubs (110142 muon, pi+) hang off the same point.
The 354.8 cm muon rises away from 14001 (64340) to a 121510 stopping end at 14000, 14001 is the lowest-z end of the event with a 2.2 cm stub attached and a scatter of small fragments around it.

The whole event is one collinear ~110 cm dashed chain (clear in the principal-frame panel) that is flat at 55-70k for 100 cm and then rises 66770 -> 118849 -> 266397 into a Bragg tip at 4000/4004, so it is a contained stopping proton and its origin is the upstream end, 54022 being the closest listed candidate there.

Rule 8: the entire event is a single straight ~17 cm MIP track (48010-48013-48011-14001-14000) with every segment flat and no second prong, so neither end is distinguishable and any click would be as good as any other.
Classic numuCC junction: a 9.5 cm proton leaves 18002 and stops at 18003 at 204467, while the 136 cm muon stays flat and exits at the x=-201 wall, so both attached particles originate here.

Rule 7 shower apex - 11028 is the upstream tip (z=198.5) of the 359 cm shower, with 2 of 3 segments rising away and a 28.8 cm electron trunk that leaves at 1.3 MIP and builds into the 196936 shower core downstream, the same signature as the other two nueCC events in this list.

The 100 cm track that stops at 11000 with a 139823 Bragg tip originates at 11004, and the big 176 cm EM shower (cluster 60) begins 4 cm away at the same point with its two 10.4 cm prongs hottest at 11004 and diluting outward.

Rule 1 in its purest form: 2 of 2 segments rise away from 2003 - a 26.5 cm proton to a 205244 Bragg stop and a 21.5 cm electron that leaves at 57465 and builds into the 257517 shower core - and 2003 is the lowest-z candidate in the event.

Same nueCC signature: a 32 cm proton leaves 11075 and terminates in a 182333 stub at 11020, while a 37 cm electron leaves at 49275 and rises x7.2 into the 354831 shower core, and 11075 is the upstream apex of the whole 734 cm cluster.

The X-Z view shows a clean V whose apex is exactly at 87155, the lowest-z point of the event; it carries the heaviest ionization present (a 7.6 cm 264681 e/cm proton stub) and a 24.7 cm prong rising away, with every other large cluster radiating downstream from it.

Rule 1: seg 9007 is a textbook proton with a monotone brown-template Bragg rise from 60k at 9002 to 205k at 9003, so it starts at the deg-3 junction 9002, which is also the lowest-z candidate (z=25) and has no segment rising toward it.

Rule 7/8 event: 30 shattered clusters with no track longer than 57 cm, and in the only coherent object (cluster 14) charge rises monotonically 14001 -> 14005 -> 14000, putting the shower apex at the low-z, low-charge end near 14001, which is the only candidate there with a rise-away and no rise-toward.

Rule 1 in its cleanest form: 2/2 segments rise away with zero rising toward, and the zoom shows two dark-red stopping hadrons (seg 17063 x6.76 to 210k, seg 17009 x1.61 to 192k) plus a MIP muon that exits at z=501, all radiating from this interior junction at z=35.
Rule 1: both attached segments rise away (10.6 cm proton to a 167k stop at 21003, 140 cm muon that leaves the detector at z=499.5), so the only junction in the event is where everything comes out of.

The 8.2 cm proton rises away x1.50 to a 215k stop at 16003 and a 129k pi+ stub sits on the same node, making 16008 the hadronic end of the long exiting muon chain; the only real competitor is 16002, 5 cm downstream, which has no hadron attached.

The event is a single 68 cm track plus sub-cm fragments; rule 1 is unambiguous between the two candidates since dQ/dx rises 67k -> 92k away from 13001, though the fact that 13001 sits exactly on the x=200 boundary makes an entering particle a real alternative reading.

Rule 1 signature at a deg-4 node: 3 of 4 segments rise away (35 cm muon, and two e prongs) with zero rising toward, and the zoom shows a genuine multi-prong star at (58,-176,277); confidence held back only because 8020/8025/8007 are alternative fragments of the same vertex region within 5 cm.

Rule 1: 2 of 3 rise away and none toward, and the zoom shows a clean 3-prong apex (74 cm muon heading down to exit the bottom, 8 cm e prong, hot 1.9 cm proton stub) with the muon cool at this end and no Bragg anywhere along it.

3002 is the most upstream junction with two prongs rising away, and the apparent rise toward it on seg 3012 is the vertex-blob trap: the p4 profile spikes only in the first cm at the junction, dips to 25k mid-segment and rises again at the 3006 end, so that particle is emitted backward from 3002 and stops at 3006.

Rule 1: 2 of 3 rise away, none toward, with a 13 cm proton stopping at 169k at 8005 and a 152k proton stub, forming a real star in the zoom; the 77 cm partner track is backward-going in z, which is the only thing arguing against it.

Rule 1 plus rule 3: the 111 cm muon rises x2.76 away from 13001 to a 123k Bragg at 13000, with two sub-cm fragments sitting right at that stopping end as a Michel, so 13000 is the far end and 13001 (which also carries a pi+ stub) is the start.

Rule 1 plus rule 3: the 133 cm muon leaves 18001 at 42.5k and Braggs at 113k at 18002 where an 11 cm Michel-like e segment hangs off, while a proton stub and the 13 cm 112k stopping proton (18004->18005) converge on the same spot in the zoom.

Two unconnected long tracks and no hadronic activity: I pick 17001 because it is the only track end that starts in the middle of the detector (the cluster-26 alternative begins exactly on the z=0 face, so that one is an entering particle), but the near-vertical direction of this track is atypical for a neutrino product.

Rule 1 plus rule 3: a 55 cm proton rises x2.02 away from 19002 to a 198k stop, the 383 cm muon runs the other way and Braggs at 115k at 19000 where three sub-cm Michel fragments sit, and 19002 is the lowest-z end of the whole chain.

Sparse event: 6001 is the interior end of the only fitted track (the other end is on the x=-200 anode), and a trail of unfitted fragments (39010, 36004) runs from it down to a 253k stopping proton stub at 37006, so the prongs converge here.

Rule 1: at this deg-3 junction the 270 cm muon and the 65.8 cm proton both get hotter going away (x2.62 to a 113985 end, x4.14 to a 206872 Bragg), and the muon's far end 3003 carries a short mu+e chain, i.e. a Michel, which by rule 3 marks it as the far end.

Rule 1: the only junction in the event with 2 of 2 segments rising away - the 256 cm muon and the 61 cm pi+ are both coolest here, and the pi+ ends in a x5.64 Bragg at 14001 surrounded by small EM fragments (pion decay/absorption); confidence capped because the whole event skims y~190-195 just under the top wall and the muon reaches the z=498 downstream wall, so a cosmic cannot be excluded.

The overview shows one unbranched 263 cm track that exits the bottom wall at y=-198.6, so the only defensible interaction point is its other, free, interior end 11001 at the lowest z; 11002 is a mid-track fit split (the 89437 spike there is the split artifact, not a Bragg), and no second prong or shower exists to confirm a neutrino at all.

The zoom shows the 6.3 cm stub and the 25.3 cm proton lying on one nearly vertical line ending in a 184783 Bragg at 8001, so they are one ~30 cm stopping proton; the dQ/dx jumps 66617 -> 124669 across 8003 (a real junction, the excess being two tracks overlapping at a vertex) but is continuous across 8004, and the 114 cm muon leaves 8003 and stops at 8002 with a Michel.

Rule 1 at the event's only deg-3 junction: the 103 cm proton rises x2.84 away to a 180157 Bragg at 17000 and the 27.6 cm muon rises x1.60 away toward a 135922 stub at 17005, with the 77 cm pi+ flat, so two of three prongs point away and none points in.

Rule 1 gives 2 of 2 rising away here: a 15.8 cm proton with a 220911 Bragg at 21000 and a 140 cm pi+ that stops at 21003, where a 14.5 cm electron segment hangs off the stopping end (decay product), marking 21003 as the far end.

The p4 profiles show the whole 129 cm chain is one particle rising monotonically from 50917 to a 197609 Bragg at 7000, so 7004 is its cool end - but 7004 sits at x=201.2, on the anode boundary, so this is an entering cosmic stopping in the detector rather than a neutrino vertex.

The 92.6 cm muon and the collinear 38.6 cm 'e' are one object whose p4 profile rises monotonically along the stopping-muon template to 130000 at 51025, so that far end is the Bragg and 6001 is the cool start - and the 1.1 cm, 228312 e/cm proton stub (cluster 44) sits 5 cm off 6001, the classic muon+proton-stub vertex.

Rule 6/7 in an all-shower event: the two shower blobs (cluster 16 at y~163-192 and cluster 93 at y~133-137) back-extrapolate to a common point near (-17,139,361), a pi0, and 90075 is the nearest candidate to it - a junction carrying a 2 cm, 100279 e/cm stub and sitting at the cool end of the 27 cm track.

The overview shows a clean V whose apex is here: a 154 cm muon Bragging at 9000 and a 108 cm proton Bragging at 16012 both start within ~11 cm of this point, and 16013 is the lower-z of the two free ends and additionally carries a 4.5 cm, 223685 e/cm stopping-proton stub.

The p4 profiles show both segments attached to 12003 start at ~94000 e/cm right at that point (a vertex charge blob) and 12003 also carries a 0.6 cm proton stub; from it a 12 cm proton rises to a 135000 Bragg at 12000 while a soft arm collapses to ~7000 toward 12007, and both arms run downstream from the cluster's minimum-z point.

Rules 1 and 3 agree: the 165.6 cm muon is at MIP (52345) here and rises x2.04 to a 106801 Bragg at 18006, where an 8.4+3.3 cm electron hangs off the stopping end as a Michel, so 18006 is the far end and 18001, which is well inside the detector, is the start.

Classic nue-CC apex: this deg-4 vertex is at the minimum z of the big cluster, the 26.5 cm electron leaves it at 37290 and rises x3.79 into the 240 cm shower downstream, and it also carries a 31 cm proton and a 29 cm track, all fanning downstream from one point.

Textbook rule 1: at this deg-3 junction the 237 cm muon rises x1.83 away to a 95279 Bragg at 14000 and the 13.7 cm proton rises x1.39 away to a 158780 Bragg at 14001, so both prongs stop elsewhere and nothing points in.

The event contains only one real object, a lone 7.4 cm stopping proton, with everything else sub-centimetre isolated dots; 7001 is its upstream end by beam direction (rule 2), but with no second prong and no shower this is close to a guess.

Rule 1: 14003 is a 44-degree kink whose muon arm shows a clean template-matching Bragg rise ending at 14001 (126645) and whose second arm is hottest at the far end 14002, so both attached tracks cool toward 14003.
Sharp V apex where a 145 cm track that stops hot at 19000 (183708) meets the stem of the EM shower that fans out to low x, with 2 of 2 segments rising away and 19002 the lowest-z point of the V.

Rule 7: the event is one big EM shower and 19001 is its apex - the lowest-z tip of a 27 cm single-MIP stem (40039 e/cm, electron not photon) that rises to 84309 where the shower blows up at 19056/19050.

4004 is the lowest-z candidate and a clean two-prong apex in the principal frame, with nothing rising toward it; the 65.8 cm MIP arm and the shower arm both open forward in z, and the two stopping protons at 4010 are 49 cm downstream at the end of that arm.

Near rule 8 - the event is only a 3.3 cm very hot (234854 e/cm) proton stub plus unconnected dots, so I take the deg-2 junction at its lower-z end as the best available click, with no directional evidence to separate the two ends.

The p4 profile of seg 23004 rises monotonically from ~20-70k at 23004 to a 160k Bragg peak near 23005, so the proton starts at 23004, which is also the deg-4 hub with three further short prongs; the 75 cm flat muon 30 cm away is unattached and shows no Bragg.
Two Bragg ends in one cluster (trap 1): the 67 cm muon follows the stopping-muon template into 16001 and the 6.5 cm prong peaks at 200k+ at 16000, and 16002 is the junction both point away from.

Rules 1 and 3 together: the 33 cm proton falls monotonically from a 300k Bragg peak at 18000 and the 22 cm muon rises along its template into 18003 where a short 8.7 cm Michel hangs off, so both prongs come out of 18002 (the shower fragments 25 cm downstream fit a pi0 gamma conversion).
Compact deg-4 hub: four prongs including a 15.6 cm proton that rises away to a 177067 Bragg end at 15001 and a 2 cm stub, with nothing rising toward it.

The 516 cm track has a genuine 95-degree corner at 14002 that no muon can scatter through, and 14002 is the local z-minimum from which both arms run forward in z (98 cm exiting the y=200 top, 413 cm ending hot at 14000).

10007 has nothing rising toward it (93 cm muon rises away to a 108123 stopping end at 10001, 11.5 cm prong rises away toward 10005) plus two short vertex stubs, and it sits 10 cm upstream of 10005 where that prong stops and the two protons star out.

Genuinely ambiguous: the dQ/dx falls monotonically from a 219257 tip at 6003 back to 1.07 MIP at the z=500.3 wall, which reads as a track stopping here (Michel-like debris cloud around it, rule 3 says far end), yet a perfectly horizontal -z cosmic is implausible and 6002 is the low-z end with a hot proton stub and all the small fragments.
Rule 1 with nothing to contradict it: the single 98 cm muon cools toward 6001 and rises to a 112800 Bragg at 6000, and 6001 is the lowest-z end and carries a short proton stub.

Extrapolating the 116 cm muon backwards from its unattached start 6001 by the 10.8 cm gap lands within 3.4 cm of 138013, the deg-3 hub of the compact hadronic blob (5.3 cm prong at 133-145k), so the muon really starts there.

Rule 8 territory - the whole event is one 8.7 cm segment plus a few sub-cm fragments in a 5 cm ball at the bottom of the detector; 15001 is the end sitting inside that fragment ball, but there is no readable direction.
